name: Phrygia
overview: Phrygia is mentioned in the Book of Acts as a significant region connected to the early spread of the gospel. It is listed among the places from which people were present at Pentecost in Jerusalem, highlighting the diverse reach of the early Christian witness (Acts 2:10). The Apostle Paul traveled through Phrygia during his missionary journeys, where he was directed by the Holy Spirit and focused on strengthening the disciples in the faith (Acts 16:6; 18:23). These references emphasize Phrygia's role as both a source of believers and a field for apostolic ministry in the expansion of the early church.
